pr_title: Fixed disappearing tilemap layers on resizing canvas(fix #2942)
pr_body:
Details of bug can be seen in #2942 -- when a change to the canvas size makes the tilemap layers disappear completely.
Referenced also in a [closed PR](https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/pull/2947).

issue_context.title: [bug] Canvas Size change makes tilemap layers disappear
issue_context.body: I just wanted to crop my image created in Aseprite 1.3 but when I did it, I realized tilemap layers are no longer rendered. 👇 Here on a screenshot below you can see how I am preparing for a canvas size change. Numbers visible on the screenshot are chosen in a way to have all layers included, so you can see how only tilemap ones are not rendered. 👇 And here is a screenshot with a canvas size change result, no tilemaps visible. ℹ️ Let me know if you need a source file from me. ### Aseprite and System version * Aseprite version: `v1.3-beta6`, from Steam * System: macOS

review_comments:
This `grid` variable has `m_origin`=(0, 0). Then `grid.canvasToTile( some canvas bound )` will result in bounds (in tile units) referred to a grid  aligned with the canvas. So, `grid.canvasToTile( some canvas bound )` in the case which the tilemap has an offset of some pixels (>0 and less than one tilesize) will result in wrong tile bounds.
Possibly you'll need to do:
`grid.origin(cel->position()); // adjust the origin of the grid`

Adjusting the `grid`'s origin here would affect the calculation of the `newPaintPos`. We only need the origin, one time, to get the right size of the new image. All the other calls to grid need the absolute positioning to work.

I didn't read all these comments, but I wanted to say that it's important to set a correct grid origin (generally the tilemap cel position, as @Gasparoken said) so `grid.canvasToTile()` and `grid.tileToCanvas()` functions work as expected (in other case converting between canvas <-> grid/tiles coordinates will not work). All the code in Aseprite is programmed in such way, and that's the expected behavior.

For example, `grid.tileToCanvas(Point(0, 0))` should return the origin position of the grid (the tilemap cel position) instead of `Point(0, 0)`. And `grid.canvasToTiles(cel->position())` should return `Point(0, 0)`.

> Adjusting the grid's origin here would affect the calculation of the newPaintPos.

From the code `paintPos` is a delta in pixels (`newCelBounds.origin() - newCelPos`) and you are converting that delta to tiles (`newPaintPos = grid.canvasToTile(paintPos)`). I can see why in this case the grid should have origin=(0,0). My personal recommendation would be that you should try to avoid converting deltas in pixels directly with the grid (it will not work). Instead you should convert canvas positions (in pixels) to tiles, and then calculating the delta of tiles (maybe something like `grid.canvasToTile(newCelBounds.origin()) - grid.canvasToTile(newCelPos)`, but I'm not sure).

Remember: to crop correctly a tilemap image through `crop_image` function, `paintPos.x`, `paintPos.y`, `newCelBounds.w`, `newCelBounds.h` these should be in tile units.

(x, y) `paintPos`  is the top-left corner tile coordinate (in tile units) from the `image` where the crop begins.

(w, h) `newCelBounds` is the size (in tile units) of the part of the `image` to being cropped.

When you do this:
```
const Tileset* tileset = static_cast<LayerTilemap*>(layer)->tileset();
grid = tileset->grid();
```
`grid.origin()` will be (0, 0) because the `static_cast<LayerTilemap*>(layer)->tile set()` doesn't return grid origin information, that's why we need to adjust the grid.origin. If you didn't adjust the `grid.origin()` the `canvasToTile` function will return incorrect coordinates.
Look at the following example:  correct `canvasToTile` return values (2x2 pixel individual tile size):
![canvasToTile](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/32165475/134707887-f458734e-0295-4847-bff3-b8ef64ef118b.gif)
This is the final adjust. My recommendation is to debug this when cases where no shrink is needed are solved.
When there's no shrink, this check `if (frameBounds != newImage->bounds())` would fail and the second cropping would not happen.
